person_note: The base narration is sustained third person, focalized chiefly through Hai and other characters across the body of the novel. Chapter 1 uses a resident-like choral first-person plural voice that calls East Gladness “our town” and addresses the arriving reader, but this isolated introductory chapter does not override the core narrative under the base-narration rule. Numerous quote passages and an authorized interior excerpt establish the continuing third-person mode, while Vuong also describes the novel broadly as third person. Dialogue, aphorisms, and embedded recollections do not create additional base strands.
